question: A 16-year-old boy is brought to the physician for a follow-up of a wound on his ankle. He had a pedestrian accident 3 days ago which caused a skin defect on the dorsal side of his left ankle. The lesion was cleaned, debrided, and observed over the past 3 days. He has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no signs of local infection. A photograph of the lesion is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate surgical management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Skin defect on dorsal side of left ankle due to pedestrian accident -> Lesion cleaned, debrided, and observed for 3 days -> No signs of local infection -> Primary closure as the most appropriate surgical management -> 95%
analysis: Based on the description provided, the wound on the boy's ankle seems to be clean, debrided, and not showing signs of infection. Considering the location and nature of the wound, primary closure would be the most appropriate surgical management option to promote optimal healing and cosmetic outcome.
